modules.note: Storage, piece table, diff, search, segments, undo, decoding. The heart of the port. Ported as of M5: the storage and document files, the text and selection files, UndoHistory, DiffEngine with DiffBlock and DiffHunkIndex, ClipboardCodec (as text/hexText.ts), and SearchEngine with SmartSearch and MatchSet — each with its upstream tests. StorageSaver does not port as a file: its POSIX strategies become src/platform/files/fileSink.ts, where the browser supplies the atomicity. SearchEngine diverges in one place worth knowing: Data.range(of:) has no JS counterpart, so the Boyer-Moore-Horspool skip loop is accelerated by native Uint8Array.indexOf on the pattern's last byte instead. Ported as of M7: SegmentWriter and SegmentReplacer, with their sizes helper (FilePaneView.friendlySize as text/byteSize.ts). SegmentWriter splits at the line D1 draws: the byte half (which range becomes which file, the chunked read, the all-or-nothing protocol) stays in core, and the filesystem half becomes a PartSink the platform layer supplies — a picked directory in Chromium, a ZIP download elsewhere. Upstream's temp-and-rename dance and its sandbox fallback have no counterpart: a browser has no rename, and createWritable() already publishes a file whole or not at all. Ported for M11: the synced collection — VersionVector, SyncedCollection, SyncMerge, SyncDocument, SearchPatternEntry and PatternLibrary, each with its upstream tests — as readonly records with functions over them; the item's Equatable and Codable are handed to the merge as SyncItemRules. The file format is upstream's field for field, because the web edition joins the Mac app's synced folder (Design/FAVORITES_SYNC_WEB.md). ContentSnapshot and TemporaryFileStore are across as contentSnapshot() over an origin-private scratch store: a browser has neither a value-typed array nor clonefile(2), so the copy is written out once rather than shared.

modules.note: Across whole at M8, with every one of its tests. Swift's protocol extensions become free functions taking a Parser, which is the same layering with the syntax the language has. Two divergences worth knowing. Reads are synchronous here as they are there, which is why parsing belongs in a worker: a worker has FileReaderSync, so six thousand lines written against synchronous reads port as they stand. And words are assembled by multiplication rather than by shifting, because JavaScript's bitwise operators are 32-bit — a dword with its top bit set comes back negative from a shift. Eight-byte fields are exact to 2^53 (every real offset and size) with a bigint path where the bits matter. Upstream's tests came across with the fixtures they need (TestImage.swift), which is what a port of a parser is checked by. One divergence the port had to find for itself: the raw-area scan finds its candidates with Uint8Array.indexOf rather than by stepping a dword along, because a loop that runs once per byte of a 32 MB image is the whole cost of a parse — measured 65 ms, then 52 with a rolled dword, then 25 with the native search (16 MB, synthetic worst case). And FV's constants live in a leaf module of their own: the scan and the volume parser import each other, which is fine for functions and not for a constant read at module load.

modules.note: The structure tree is across at M8: a virtualised list rather than an NSOutlineView, with the same lazy expansion — a region's raw-area scan and a volume's file walk are never run until a row is opened. LazyUEFITree's actor becomes a worker plus a store: the worker holds the ImageReader and answers roots, children, the node at an offset, details and repairs; the store holds the tree React renders. The panel follows UEFIToolViewController's layout: the title with the wrapper root folded into it and the reveal-at-caret button, the Name/Type/Subtype tree over the detail with a divider the reader moves (the detail starts at a third), a branch that stays shut until it arrives with a Loading… row only after 200 ms, and the notice line. UEFITreeDisplay and UEFINodeDetail are ported with their tests; the column texts and the detail are built in the worker, where the parsed node and the reader are, and the name on the main thread, where the GUID catalogue is. The tree dresses its rows with the shared row marks and carries the panel's legend (ROW_MARKS.md; UEFITreeMarks.swift, uefiTreeMarks.ts). Divergences: the detail has no "Decompressed from" row (compressed sections are not ported), so no row wears the rail (G1) and no node is placed inside a protected range, so none is tinted (G3) — the legend lists neither, and the two vendor hash tables are the only holders of checks, the Insyde arm being unported (G6). Column widths are fixed rather than draggable, and the rows the reader had open travel in the panel's parked session state rather than in the pane (G12). The row menu is the one command upstream offers and only on a node whose checksum is wrong, through the document, so Cmd/Ctrl+Z takes it back.

One overlay serves files and panes both, as upstream's does: the bands mean the same either way, so there is one geometry and one set of handlers and only the captions differ. The AppKit half of that overlay — its `dragging*` overrides, its pasteboard types, its testing seams — becomes the region `paneDropRegion` plus `paneDragStore`, because a browser hides a drag's payload from every `dragover` and so the pane in flight has to be held outside the drag. One declaration is left out on the owner's instruction: NewTabDropStrip, the strip along the top of the window, and with it the `Destination.newTabStrip` and `Outcome.tearOff` arms that only it can produce; a pane's drag between browser tabs is notApplicable.

modules.note: The comparison readout as a share of the longer file: the extent, the differing bytes, and "differing 12.3%" rounded up to a tenth of a percent — empty when nothing differs, because 0.0% would read as a comparison that is not running. The value and the line it goes into live in one web file, where upstream keeps the struct beside the labels `ComparisonView.refreshComparisonInfo` writes onto; the pane asks for the text as it draws (`comparisonInfo`). The sum upstream writes as a reduce over `index.blocks` is `DiffBlockIndex.differingBytes`, which walks the index's flat columns.

The sheet an operation that blocks its pane runs under: the same BackgroundOperation the pane's status strip shows, presented over the window with Cancel as its button and Esc as its key equivalent, and closed by the operation finishing. Update in Parent is not ported (G4), and the web edition shows a running operation in the pane's own strip — src/ui/pane/OperationStrip.tsx — which has no modal sheet.

modules.note: The frosted plate over the window, one at a time: the wrap glyph a step or a first-hit scan shows when it came round an end, and the list a Smart Search that found nothing names its encodings in. Upstream's hold and fade timings; a new plate replaces the last at once, a stale one fades, and starting a search or closing the bar takes it away. Drawn with pointer-events: none, glyphs as inline SVG. The plate's grey is NoticeColors.icon (--notice-icon): the glyph and every line under it are the same colour on purpose — a plate is one object, and a sign louder than its own text would read as two (G42). The plate is a square, with the glyph above its lines and the whole thing centred: the side is whatever the content asked for, and the cap on a window too narrow for it wins over the square, as upstream's preferred heightAnchor == widthAnchor gives way to the presenter's width cap. That is the stylesheet's `aspect-ratio: 1` on .transient-notice, with upstream's `inset` as its padding, `cornerRadius` as its radius and `glyphToTextSpacing` as its gap, and the two glyph sizes are TransientNotice.tsx's SYMBOL_SIZE (72) and GLYPH_SIZE (76), upstream's own numbers (G44). The case that holds the shape is SmartSearchFlowTests' testTheNoticeIsCentredAndSitsInTheLowerThird, which reads the laid-out box back and so stays `later`.

A panel's scrolling detail: title, label/value rows with one label width, and the tables after them, on the panel's own ground, scrolled back to the top only when the subject changes.
